claims.statement: Commission remuneration remained prevalent in 24 Member States in 2024, and agents and brokers were the main distribution channel in most Member States.
Poland had 28,365 registered insurance agents and 1,418 insurance brokers at the end of 2024.

The registry counts are only an upper bound: KNF's agent definition includes businesses with different carrier relationships, and the sources do not identify active multi-carrier agencies with material reconciliation complexity.
SuperAgent says an agency can upload original carrier commission files, automate settlement for each insurer, and buy the product from tens of PLN per month.
SuperBroker already imports commission notes from all insurers, checks carrier-paid commission against internal records, tracks discrepancy explanations, and lists 99-199 PLN monthly pricing.
Berg System advertises the same month-end insurer-note import, commission reports, and commission-settlement system, while KA System reports meaningful use of commission-processing functionality.

Because Polish incumbents already own the workflow at low bundled prices, a standalone overlay must prove incremental recovered value or substantially better exception accuracy; generic reconciliation is not a sufficient paid wedge.
A customer can lawfully appoint an external SaaS provider as a processor when a binding contract, documented instructions, confidentiality, security, and subprocessor controls are in place.

KNF treats cloud processing of legally protected financial-sector information as a governed outsourcing risk; this raises assurance and onboarding costs but does not show that the required right is unobtainable.
Applied Systems' 2026 embedded reconciliation product shows that a broker-management incumbent can absorb carrier-statement ingestion and matching into the system of record.
A broker-software reseller strategy is not presently supported: the identified vendors are potential competitors with overlapping products, and no partner commitment or referral economics are public.
No located public Polish evidence quantifies recurring carrier underpayment, mismatch rates, recovery rates, or administrator hours after use of current agency and broker systems.

It is unknown whether each target customer has contractual permission, complete expected-rate schedules, stable policy identifiers, and export rights sufficient for an independent expected-versus-paid calculation.
Observed incumbent prices make the original 400-2,500 PLN monthly assumption weak; a 199-499 PLN monthly overlay is a more conservative test range until incremental recovery is demonstrated.

At 500 accounts paying 250 PLN monthly, ARR would be 1.5m PLN and a 25% owner-cash margin would be 375,000 PLN per mature year; this does not support the original rapid wealth path without higher proven ARPU or expansion.
A two-format batch pilot appears compatible with the founder's capital and time only if exception handling is tightly capped; actual security, mapping, and support cost remains unknown.

Generic document parsing is reproducible; defensibility would have to come from a permissioned adjudicated exception corpus and adoption of the audit ledger in the payout workflow, neither of which is currently evidenced.

contrary_evidence: Low-priced Polish products already import original insurer commission files and automate settlement.
Two Polish broker systems explicitly advertise expected-versus-paid verification, commission reports, and discrepancy handling.
A major global broker-management incumbent has embedded similar reconciliation inside its system of record.
The public Polish registry denominator does not isolate the economically relevant multi-carrier subset.
